title: Expand to new clients without losing exclusivity
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Expand to new clients without losing exclusivity.

Who it is for: A heritage watchmaker whose clients are mostly over 55.
The numbers: Its clients spend Rs 12 lakh a year on average; it wins only 300 new ones a year.
The catch: Every new client must feel as exclusive as the old ones; one mass campaign could undo 40 years of the brand.
You win if: 1,000 new clients in a year with no fall in the average price paid.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: One personal assistant for a client's whole luxury life
body:
Luxury · Round 3. One personal assistant for a client's whole luxury life.

Who it is for: A family that spends on travel, fashion, art and cars through 20 separate concierges.
The numbers: They spend about Rs 3 crore a year and lose roughly 40 hours a month to arranging it.
The catch: They share their data with no one they do not trust completely.
You win if: One assistant they use every week, and a fee they pay without asking for a discount.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Prove any luxury item is genuine in seconds
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Prove any luxury item is genuine in seconds.

Who it is for: Resale shops and buyers of second-hand luxury bags and watches.
The numbers: 1 in 8 items offered for resale is fake, and an expert check takes 3 days and costs Rs 4,000.
The catch: Counterfeits now pass the checks experts use, so a better eye is not enough.
You win if: A check in under 60 seconds, at under Rs 200, that catches 99% of fakes.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Fractional ownership of art, cars or watches
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Fractional ownership of art, cars or watches.

Who it is for: Young professionals who earn well but cannot buy a Rs 50 lakh painting or car.
The numbers: A share can start at Rs 25,000, and a year of ownership must cost less than renting the item.
The catch: Owners argue about who uses the car, when to sell and who pays for insurance.
You win if: Shares that sell again within a week at a fair price, with no disputes left open.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: After-sales care as good as the purchase
body:
Luxury · Round 3. After-sales care as good as the purchase.

Who it is for: Clients who bought a Rs 5 lakh piece and waited 3 months for a repair.
The numbers: Repairs take 90 days on average and 30% of clients do not buy again after one.
The catch: The best craftsmen are few, and are in Europe.
You win if: Repairs back in under 14 days and clients who buy again more often after a repair than before it.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Turn a fashion brand into a hospitality experience
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Turn a fashion brand into a hospitality experience.

Who it is for: A fashion house that wants clients to stay, eat and celebrate inside its world.
The numbers: A hotel costs Rs 200 crore to build; the brand has Rs 20 crore to spend.
The catch: Hospitality is a different business, and one bad stay is seen by the whole fashion world.
You win if: A first experience that sells out and earns money within 12 months.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Luxury materials that are fully traceable and sustainable
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Luxury materials that are fully traceable and sustainable.

Who it is for: Brands that use leather, gold and silk and are asked where they came from.
The numbers: Under 20% of their materials can be traced to the source today.
The catch: Suppliers guard their sources, and new materials must still feel luxurious.
You win if: 80% of materials traced, with proof a client can see on the product.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Win the next generation of luxury buyers
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Win the next generation of luxury buyers.

Who it is for: Buyers aged 22 to 30 who prefer experiences, resale and their own feeds to the brand's store.
The numbers: They will be 40% of luxury buyers by 2030 but are 10% of this brand's sales.
The catch: What attracts them may put off today's loyal clients.
You win if: Doubling the brand's sales to buyers under 30 without losing its older clients.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Private, secure data for high-net-worth clients
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Private, secure data for high-net-worth clients.

Who it is for: Families whose wealth, travel and purchases are tracked by apps, staff and hackers.
The numbers: One leak can cost a client crores in fraud or kidnap risk.
The catch: Clients want privacy and the convenience of apps at the same time.
You win if: A service clients trust with their data, audited by an outside firm, that nobody leaves.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Circular luxury: repair, resell and refurbish at scale
body:
Luxury · Round 3. Circular luxury: repair, resell and refurbish at scale.

Who it is for: A luxury group with 50,000 old pieces in its clients' cupboards.
The numbers: Each piece can be repaired and resold 2 or 3 times; today 5% are.
The catch: Resale must not make new pieces look cheaper.
You win if: Resale and repair worth 15% of the group's revenue within 3 years.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Cut fresh-food waste from 9% to 3% across the supply chain
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Cut fresh-food waste from 9% to 3% across the supply chain.

Who it is for: A dairy and fresh-produce brand that sells through 30,000 shops.
The numbers: 9% of its fresh stock is thrown away, worth Rs 60 crore a year.
The catch: Shops do not share their sales data and have no space for new equipment.
You win if: Waste at 3% within a year, with shops earning more than before.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Reach 50,000 rural kirana shops profitably
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Reach 50,000 rural kirana shops profitably.

Who it is for: A biscuit and soap company that sells in cities but hardly reaches villages.
The numbers: A rural kirana orders Rs 2,000 a week, and each delivery costs Rs 300.
The catch: Roads, cash payments and tiny orders make every visit expensive.
You win if: 50,000 shops served at a profit on every order within 18 months.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Plastic-free packaging that costs under Rs 1 more per pack
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Plastic-free packaging that costs under Rs 1 more per pack.

Who it is for: A snacks brand selling 2 crore packs a month.
The numbers: Plastic packaging costs Rs 1.20 a pack; the alternatives cost Rs 3 or more.
The catch: Food must stay fresh for 6 months in hot, humid shops.
You win if: Plastic-free packs at under Rs 2.20 a pack with the same shelf life.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Honest health labels shoppers actually read
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Honest health labels shoppers actually read.

Who it is for: Shoppers who spend 4 seconds choosing a pack of noodles.
The numbers: Under 10% read the label, and most claims on the front are vague.
The catch: Brands fear honest labels will hurt sales.
You win if: A label that changes what at least 1 shopper in 5 buys, with sales held.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Forecast festival demand within 10% across city types
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Forecast festival demand within 10% across city types.

Who it is for: A sweets and snacks brand planning Diwali.
The numbers: Last year it overstocked metros by 40% and ran out in small towns, a Rs 3.2 crore loss.
The catch: Every city and town celebrates differently, and data from small shops is thin.
You win if: A forecast within 10% in every city type, tested on last year's festival.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Win shelf space on quick-commerce apps against big brands
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Win shelf space on quick-commerce apps against big brands.

Who it is for: A new healthy-food brand on quick-commerce apps.
The numbers: The top 3 brands take 80% of the first screen, and paying for placement costs 25% of sales.
The catch: The apps own the customer data and change their rankings often.
You win if: First-screen placement in 3 cities while spending under 10% of sales on it.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Make healthy snacks affordable under Rs 20
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Make healthy snacks affordable under Rs 20.

Who it is for: Students and workers who buy snacks at Rs 10 to Rs 20.
The numbers: Healthy snacks today cost Rs 50 or more.
The catch: Better ingredients cost more, and cheap healthy snacks often taste worse.
You win if: A healthy snack at Rs 20 that sells 1 lakh packs a month and earns a margin.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Trace every ingredient from farm to pack in seconds
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Trace every ingredient from farm to pack in seconds.

Who it is for: A spice and tea company with 4,000 farmers.
The numbers: Tracing a single ingredient today takes 3 weeks and a phone call to each supplier.
The catch: Farmers have basic phones, and middlemen do not want to be seen.
You win if: Every pack traceable to its farms in under 10 seconds.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Return and refill systems for household products
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Return and refill systems for household products.

Who it is for: City households that buy detergent, shampoo and oil in plastic bottles.
The numbers: A family throws away about 150 bottles a year.
The catch: Refills must be no harder and no dearer than buying a new bottle.
You win if: 20,000 households refilling every month and 30% less plastic sold.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Personalised nutrition for India's diabetic population
body:
FMCG · Round 3. Personalised nutrition for India's diabetic population.

Who it is for: Some of India's 10 crore people with diabetes, and their families.
The numbers: Most see a doctor twice a year and get the same generic diet chart.
The catch: Food is cultural, budgets are tight, and nobody wants to feel ill.
You win if: Members whose blood sugar improves measurably within 6 months, at under Rs 500 a month.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Rooftop solar for renters and apartment blocks
body:
Energy · Round 3. Rooftop solar for renters and apartment blocks.

Who it is for: Renters and apartment residents who cannot put panels on a roof they do not own.
The numbers: Half of city homes are rented or in tall blocks.
The catch: Owners, residents' associations and the power company must all agree.
You win if: 500 flats on solar in a year, with tenants saving 20% on their bills.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: EV charging on highways that pays for itself in 3 years
body:
Energy · Round 3. EV charging on highways that pays for itself in 3 years.

Who it is for: Highway charging-station investors.
The numbers: A fast charger costs Rs 40 lakh and sees only 6 cars a day today.
The catch: Highway traffic is seasonal and EV numbers are still small.
You win if: A site that pays back in 3 years with today's traffic.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Batteries that survive Indian summers for 10 years
body:
Energy · Round 3. Batteries that survive Indian summers for 10 years.

Who it is for: Home and shop battery owners in North India.
The numbers: Batteries lose half their life in 45°C heat.
The catch: Cooling uses the power the battery is meant to save.
You win if: Batteries that keep 80% of their capacity after 10 hot summers, at no more than 15% extra cost.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Carbon tracking a small factory can afford
body:
Energy · Round 3. Carbon tracking a small factory can afford.

Who it is for: Small factories that export to Europe and must report their carbon.
The numbers: A carbon audit costs Rs 5 lakh; most factories earn Rs 2 crore a year.
The catch: Factory owners have no data team and do not trust software.
You win if: A report that buyers accept, for under Rs 25,000 a year.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Cutting peak-hour demand without blackouts
body:
Energy · Round 3. Cutting peak-hour demand without blackouts.

Who it is for: A city power company that buys expensive power at 7 pm every summer evening.
The numbers: Peak power costs 4× normal, and a 10% cut would avoid blackouts.
The catch: Nobody wants to be told when to use their AC.
You win if: Peak demand down 10% with no blackouts and no forced switch-offs.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Clean cooking for 20 crore rural homes
body:
Energy · Round 3. Clean cooking for 20 crore rural homes.

Who it is for: Rural homes still cooking on wood and dung.
The numbers: Smoke from cooking harms health in millions of homes; an LPG refill costs a week's income.
The catch: Families go back to wood when gas runs out or gets dear.
You win if: 10,000 homes cooking clean every day after a year, not only on day one.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Recycling used EV and solar batteries
body:
Energy · Round 3. Recycling used EV and solar batteries.

Who it is for: Owners of used EV batteries and old solar panels.
The numbers: 1 lakh tonnes of batteries will retire each year by 2030; under 10% are recycled properly.
The catch: Informal recyclers pay more and pollute.
You win if: A recycling route that pays owners as much as the informal trade and recovers 90% of the metals.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Green power for cold storage on farms
body:
Energy · Round 3. Green power for cold storage on farms.

Who it is for: Farmers' cooperatives that store fruit and vegetables.
The numbers: Up to 30% of produce rots for lack of cold storage; diesel cold rooms cost Rs 1,500 a day to run.
The catch: Villages have power for only part of the day.
You win if: Cold storage running on clean power at half the cost of diesel.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Paying households for power they save
body:
Energy · Round 3. Paying households for power they save.

Who it is for: Households on a city power network.
The numbers: The power company pays Rs 12 for a unit at peak and sells it to homes at Rs 7.
The catch: Saving must be easy and the payment worth noticing.
You win if: 50,000 homes paid every month, with savings the power company can measure.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.

title: Clean energy for 24/7 data centres
body:
Energy · Round 3. Clean energy for 24/7 data centres.

Who it is for: Data-centre operators that promise clients clean power at every hour.
The numbers: Solar covers the day; nights and cloudy weeks still run on coal.
The catch: Storage for every hour is very expensive.
You win if: 90% clean power around the clock at a price clients accept.

Design the solution, how it is delivered and how it is measured.
